trust_decision.summary: Whether the caller of GET /cosmos/api/constellation/public-devices is an authenticated user; at the pinned commit the handler only checks that an Authorization header is non-empty and never validates it, and the admin subrouter has no auth middleware of its own (each handler must call utils.CheckPermissions).

landing_point.why: The advisory names the public-devices endpoint and bearer tokens; DevicePublicList is its only HTTP handler and the bogus header check sits in its first lines.

fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP handler (legacy endpoint, same module as landing point)

fix_sites.entry_point: any proxied route with constellation tunnel auth bypass (tokenMiddleware); same commit, changelog 'Only allow manager server to bypass tunnel authorization' (fix.diff:484) - a separate protection, not the advisory's endpoint
helper GetConstellationFromIP added to src/constellation/index.go for the routerGen change; no entry point of its own

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/constellation/api_devices_public.go:109-171 (PublicDeviceListNATS, a second implementation of the same device listing over NATS) is protected by NATS per-device credentials (src/constellation/NATS.go user list built from CachedDevices APIKey) and was not changed; it is not an unprotected route

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Only weak: a solver could argue the NATS responder PublicDeviceListNATS is a separate transport already gated by NATS credentials, which is true, so there is nothing real to dismiss.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Cluster nodes still need the device list: the NATS subject cosmos._global_.constellation.public-devices must keep answering authenticated NATS peers; an over-broad fix that removes or gates the shared listing logic breaks constellation sync. Logged-in non-admin users (PERM_LOGIN) must still get the HTTP list, so requiring admin/PERM_RESOURCES would be over-broad.

O6_input_shapes: missing Authorization header (already rejected at pinned commit)
arbitrary non-empty Authorization value / arbitrary Bearer string (accepted at pinned commit; rejected by CheckPermissions after fix)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a thin wrapper in package constellation that delegates to a pro.* handler without calling utils.CheckPermissions, relying on the delegate to check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pinned code already delegates every deployments route to src/pro/api_deployments.go stubs that do no permission check themselves; a maintainer adding the OSS implementation could easily assume the wrapper or the other side checks.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a device-facing handler that, like the old public-devices code, accepts any device-style bearer token instead of validating it via CheckConstellationToken or CheckPermissions
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Device-to-server endpoints in this package mix device API-key auth (src/constellation/api_nebula.go:16-55) and user auth (CheckPermissions); a handler written for agents could plausibly stop at a non-empty header check, as DevicePublicList did.

O9_family: missing authentication on an HTTP handler (CWE-287, A07): header presence checked, value never validated

O10_build.toolchain: Go toolchain (go.mod at repo root); React client in client/ is not needed for the backend handler
services: embedded DB collection via utils.GetEmbeddedCollection (needed for the device list)
O10_build.project_tests: No *_test.go files in src/constellation or src/proxy at the pinned commit; no project tests for this area.

j.j_sites_touched: src/constellation/api_devices_public.go (advisory); same commit also src/proxy/routerGen.go, src/constellation/index.go (tunnel bypass, separate protection)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add utils.CheckPermissions(w, req, utils.PERM_LOGIN) at the top of DevicePublicList - which is exactly the published fix, so there is no tempting wrong fix.

out_of_scope_notes: src/proxy/routerGen.go:52-65 tunnel auth bypass for any constellation device (fixed in the same commit to manager-only, CosmosNode == 2); a separate protection with a different sink.

src/proxy/shield.go:297-307 GetClientID trusts X-Forwarded-For from any constellation device with a valid token; this is client identity for SmartShield, not the advisory's protection, and the fix did not change it.
unverified: Latest release is 'none', so present_in_latest could not be checked.
Not checked whether CosmosNode value 2 means 'manager' in every code path; inferred from src/constellation/api_devices_create.go:250-276 and the fix's own use.

All other handlers registered in src/constellation were grepped for a CheckPermissions call; DNSEntriesRoute and ConstellationAPIDevices dispatch to sub-handlers that do check (src/constellation/api_dns.go:44, src/constellation/api_devices_list.go:26, src/constellation/api_devices_create.go:73). Handlers registered through pro.RegisterRoutes (src/httpServer.go:770) were not audited.
